226923.l: Parisotoma notabilis is a species of elongate-bodied springtail in the family Isotomidae. It can be found in both Europe and North America, with four distinct lineages differing significantly in both mitochondrial and nuclear genetics. The species reproduces by parthenogenesis.

226924.l: Pseudosorensia is a genus of springtails belonging to the family Isotomidae. The genus was first recognised by Dora Esther Cutini de Izarra in 1972.

226925.l: Pseudosorensia atlantica is a species of springtail belonging to the family Isotomidae. The species was first described by Keith Arthur John Wise in 1970, and is found in South Georgia.

226927.l: Cryptopygus is a genus of springtails. Cryptopygus belongs to the Isotomidae family.

226928.l: Cryptopygus agreni is a species of springtail in the genus Cryptopygus. It is sometime considered a synonym for Hemisotoma pontica (Stach, 1947)

226929.l: Cryptopygus antarcticus, the Antarctic springtail, is a species of springtail native to Antarctica and Australia. Cryptopygus antarcticus average long and weigh only a few micrograms. Like other springtails, the Antarctic springtail has been found to be useful as a bioindicator of pollution and has been used to study microplastic pollution in Antarctica. They also tend aggregate, by signaling to other individuals via pheromones, especially when temperatures are low, to avoid a high water loss rate.

226930.cap: Holotype of Cryptopygus campbellensis from the collections of Te Papa
226930.l: Cryptopygus campbellensis is a species of springtail belonging to the family Isotomidae. The species was first described by Keith Arthur John Wise in 1964. The species is native to Campbell Island in the New Zealand Subantarctic Islands.

226931.l: Cryptopygus cisantarcticus is a species of springtail belonging to the family Isotomidae. The species was first described by Keith Arthur John Wise in 1967. The species is native to the Cape Hallett area of Northern Victoria Land in East Antarctica and the surrounding offshore islands, including the Balleny Islands.

226932.l: Cryptopygus elegans is a species of springtails found in Argentina.

226933.l: Cryptopygus nivicolus is a species of springtail native to Antarctica. It is found in southern Victoria Land.

226934.l: Cryptopygus terranovus is a species of springtail belonging to the family Isotomidae. The species was first described by Keith Arthur John Wise in 1967, and is found on Antarctica.

226935.l: Anurophorus is a genus of Collembola belonging to the family Isotomidae.

226936.l: Proisotominae is a subfamily of elongate-bodied springtails in the family Isotomidae. There are about 7 genera and more than 190 described species in Proisotominae.

226937.l: Folsomia is a genus of elongate-bodied springtails in the family Isotomidae. There are more than 110 described species in Folsomia.

226938.l: Folsomia candida is a species of springtail in the family Isotomidae. It is found in soil in many locations around the world, having been spread inadvertently by humans. It reproduces by parthenogenesis and has been used as a model organism in research.

226939.l: Folsomia fimetaria is an elongate-bodied springtail of the genus Folsomia. It differs from other members of the Folsomia genus, in that the ventral setae on the third segment of the thorax are absent. It its maxillary head their lamella 1 is fan-shaped and has a double fringe, also its apical row has complex cilia. F. fimetaria inhabits in rich organic soils, disturbed biotopes and cities. It also seems to be a high-quality prey, since, when eaten by Bembidion lampros they seem to improve their fecundity and their larval survival.

226940.l: Folsomia prima is a species of elongate-bodied springtails in the family Isotomidae.

226941.l: Folsomia regularis is a species of elongate-bodied springtails in the family Isotomidae.

226942.l: Proisotoma is a genus of elongate-bodied springtails in the family Isotomidae. There are at least 50 described species in Proisotoma.

226943.l: Proisotoma minuta is a species of elongate-bodied springtail in the family Isotomidae. It is found in Europe. It has also been found in agricultural land in Manitoba, Canada. This species is a fungivore.

226945.l: Desoria elegans is a species of springtail from Switzerland.

226946.l: Desoria klovstadi is a species of springtail native to Antarctica. It was one of the first Antarctic species, from the class of Collembola, to be described.

226947.cap: A group of glacier fleas assembled on the Tiefenbachferner, Tyrol, Austria
226947.l: The glacier flea is a group of glacial springtail. D. saltans is the most famous species of glacier flea, the first one described (Nicolet, 1841) but there are several springtail species that are also called glacier fleas, and which catch the attention on snow surfaces due to their dark body colouring, their hopping motion and the fact that they often gather in large groups.

226948.l: Antarcticinella is a genus of springtails native to Antarctica. It is monotypic, being represented by the single species Antarcticinella monoculata. The genus and species were original described by John Salmon in 1965.

226949.l: Antarcticinella is a genus of springtails native to Antarctica. It is monotypic, being represented by the single species Antarcticinella monoculata. The genus and species were original described by John Salmon in 1965.

226951.l: Hydroisotoma schaefferi is a springtail native to the eastern US.

226952.l: Isotomodes is a genus of arthropods belonging to the family Isotomidae.

226953.l: Cryptopygus is a genus of springtails. Cryptopygus belongs to the Isotomidae family.

226954.l: Vertagopus is a genus of springtails belonging to the family Isotomidae.

226955.l: The Entomobryomorpha are one of the three main orders of springtails (Collembola), tiny hexapods related to insects. This group was formerly treated as a superfamily, the Entomobryoidea.

226957.l: Tomocerus is a genus of springtails described by Nicolet in 1841.

226958.l: Tomocerus minor is a species of springtail in the family Tomoceridae. It is widespread from the Arctic to Europe, Western and Central Asia down to the Sino-Japanese, Northern and Pacific North America, Hawaii, the Caribbean mainland and New Zealand.

226959.l: Tomocerus vulgaris is a species of elongate-bodied springtail in the family Tomoceridae. It is found in Europe.

226960.l: Plutomurus is a genus of springtails belonging to the family Tomoceridae.

226961.sd: Species of springtail that is the deepest terrestrial animal ever found on Earth
226961.l: Plutomurus ortobalaganensis is the deepest terrestrial animal ever found on Earth, living at below a cave entrance. It is a species of springtail (arthropods) endemic to the Krubera-Voronja cave system in Abkhazia, Georgia. It was discovered in the CAVEX Team expedition of 2010. It feeds on a few fungi and decomposing organic matter in the caves.

226962.l: Pogonognathellus is a genus of arthropods belonging to the family Tomoceridae.

226963.l: Pogonognathellus longicornis (former names: Tomocerus longicornis or Podura longicornis) is a common species of springtail present in Europe.

226964.l: Tomolonus is a monotypic genus of springtail in the family Tomoceridae, containing only the species Tomolonus reductus. It is similar to the other members of Tomoceridae, but is distinguished by having only 3 ocelli on its eyepatch. The genus was first described by the American entomologist Harlow B. Mills in 1949.

226965.l: Tomolonus is a monotypic genus of springtail in the family Tomoceridae, containing only the species Tomolonus reductus. It is similar to the other members of Tomoceridae, but is distinguished by having only 3 ocelli on its eyepatch. The genus was first described by the American entomologist Harlow B. Mills in 1949.

226966.l: The order Poduromorpha is one of the three main groups of springtails (Collembola), tiny hexapods related to insects. This group was formerly treated as a superfamily Poduroidea.

226967.l: Hypogastruridae is a family of springtails. Members of the family are common and widespread with a cosmopolitan distribution of about 660 species in about 40 genera.

226968.l: Ceratophysella is a genus of springtails and allies in the family Hypogastruridae. There are at least 100 described species in Ceratophysella.

226969.m: Mushroom springtail, Comox Valley, BC, Canada imported from iNaturalist photo 532601657.jpg
226969.l: Ceratophysella denticulata, the mushroom springtail, is a species of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae.

226970.l: Ceratophysella gibbosa is a species of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae.

226971.l: Ceratophysella pratorum is a species of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae.

226972.l: Ceratophysella succinea is a species of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae.

226973.l: Hypogastrura is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are at least 150 described species in the genus. Their name means ‘lack of a stomach tail’.

226974.l: Hypogastrura harveyi, the snow flea, is a species of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae.

226975.cap: A Hypogastrura manubrialis magnified by a hundred times
226975.l: Hypogastrura manubrialis is a species of springtail in the family Hypogastruridae.

226976.l: Hypogastrura nivicola is a species of dark blue springtail. Its English name in the United States is snow flea, but there are also additional springtails (and insects) called by that name. They are unrelated to the more commonly known flea.

226977.l: Hypogastrura tooliki, the toolik snow flea, is a species of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae.

226978.l: Cosberella is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are about eight described species in Cosberella.

226979.l: Cosberella denali is a springtail species of the family Hypogastruridae. It is endemic to Alaska. Arne Fjellberg, who first described the species in 1985, theorized three potential subspecies based on significant morphological differences – one each found in the Alaska Range, the Brooks Range, and the Alaska North Slope.

226980.l: Cosberella lamaralexanderi, or the Lamar Alexander springtail, is a species of springtails native to the southern Appalachian Mountains of the United States.

226981.l: Schaefferia is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are at least 20 described species in Schaefferia.

226982.l: Schaefferia duodecimocellata is a species of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae.

226983.l: Schaefferia profundissima is a species of springtail (arthropods) endemic to the Krubera-Voronja cave system in Georgia. It is one of the deepest terrestrial animal ever found on Earth, living at > below the cave entrance. It was discovered in the CAVEX Team expedition of 2010.

226984.l: Xenylla is a genus of springtails and allies in the family Hypogastruridae. There are at least 120 described species in Xenylla.

226985.l: Xenylla grisea is a species of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae.

226986.l: Xenylla littoralis is a species of springtail of the family Hypogastruridae described in 1933 by the English entomologist Herbert Womersley. Its description is in the records of the South Australian Museum.

226987.l: Gomphiocephalus is a genus of springtail native to Antarctica. Gomphiocephalus hodgsoni is the only member of the genus.

226988.l: Gomphiocephalus is a genus of springtail native to Antarctica. Gomphiocephalus hodgsoni is the only member of the genus.

226989.l: Acherongia is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are at least four described species in Acherongia.

226990.l: Acherontides is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are about 11 described species in Acherontides.

226991.l: Acherontiella is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are at least 20 described species in Acherontiella.

226992.l: Acheroxenylla is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are at least three described species in Acheroxenylla.

226993.l: Austrogastrura is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are at least three described species in Austrogastrura.

226994.l: Barbagastrura is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There is at least one described species in Barbagastrura, B. palpigera.

226995.l: Biscoia is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There is at least one described species in Biscoia, B. sudpolaris.

226996.l: Bonetogastrura is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are about seven described species in Bonetogastrura.

226997.l: Celegastrura is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There is at least one described species in Celegastrura, C. aldebaranis.

226998.l: Choreutinula is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There are about five described species in Choreutinula.

226999.l: Denigastrura is a genus of springtails in the family Hypogastruridae. There is at least one described species in Denigastrura, D. tetrophthalma.
